You must hire exactly one candidate from a pool of 100, interviewing them one at a time in random order, deciding to accept or reject immediately with no recall of anyone rejected. The strategy that maximizes your chance of picking the single best candidate is to automatically reject an initial sample, then accept the next candidate who beats everyone seen so far. Roughly what fraction of the pool should that initial 'reject no matter what' sample be?

Benford's Law describes the distribution of leading (first) digits in many naturally occurring numerical datasets, such as populations, stock prices, and physical constants. Which leading digit actually occurs most often?
choices: Every digit is equally likely, about 11.1% each

questions.q: Three identical-looking boxes: one holds two gold coins, one holds two silver coins, and one holds one gold and one silver coin. You pick a box at random and draw one of its coins at random — it turns out to be gold. What is the probability the OTHER coin in that same box is also gold?
A cereal brand puts 1 of 6 different toys in every box, each toy equally likely. Buying boxes one at a time until you own all 6 toys, about how many boxes should you expect to need on average?

A single-elimination tournament starts with 127 players. Matches are played one at a time; each match has exactly two players, and the loser is eliminated immediately. This continues until only one player — the champion — remains. How many matches are played in total?
A rooster lays an egg on the exact peak of a barn roof. Which side does the egg roll down?

In a doubling ('Martingale') betting strategy on a fair coin, you bet $1 and double your next bet after every loss, stopping as soon as you win once. Assuming no table limit and unlimited money, what is your profit when you finally win?
choices: $1, no matter how many losses came before it
It depends on how many times you lost first
A net loss equal to the total amount wagered
$0, since it's a fundamentally fair game

questions.q: You are running a race and you overtake the person in second place. What position are you in now?
choices: It depends on the length of the race

questions.q: You answer 10 independent true/false questions, and you are perfectly well-calibrated at 90% confidence on each one. What is the probability you get all 10 correct?
A man walks into a bar and asks the bartender for a glass of water. The bartender pulls out a gun and points it at him. The man says 'thank you' and calmly walks out. Why?
choices: The man was testing whether the gun was loaded
The bartender recognised him as a wanted criminal
The man had hiccups, and the shock of the gun cured them
The bartender was joking with a water pistol
